articles.title: Confessions Of A Messier Marathoner
articles.summary: The author initially expressed skepticism about the competitive nature of a Messier Marathon but recounts their experience at an event at Henry Coe park. Despite initial cloudy and windy weather, spirits were high among 25-plus participants who sighted Comet Hale-Bopp. The marathon then began with clear skies, as the author used a 6" f/8 Cave reflector, noting that aperture size seemed to make little difference.

articles.title: Activities Calendar
articles.summary: This document outlines a calendar of astronomical activities and club events for April and May. It details various star parties, astronomy classes, and general meetings at locations like Houge Park, Fremont Peak, and Henry Coe. The calendar also notes larger events such as the Texas Star Party, Riverside Telescope Makers Conference, and a Bay-Area Swap Meet, including details like moon phases and sunset times.

articles.title: Small Aperture Messier Hunting
articles.summary: Jay Freeman recounts his "Messier survey" observations over a March weekend, utilizing small aperture instruments like 10x50 binoculars, a 50mm refractor, and a modified 98mm Brandon refractor at Fremont Peak and Henry Coe State Park. He details the unusual history of his Brandon 98mm scope, which was originally a 94mm model with its aperture enlarged by a previous owner. The article focuses on personal observing experiences with specific equipment.

articles.title: SJAA Bay Area Swap Meet And Auction This Month!
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) is hosting its periodic Bay Area Swap Meet and Auction on Saturday, April 19, at Houge Park convention center, starting at noon with the auction following at 4 pm. Attendees can buy and sell a wide range of amateur astronomy equipment, components, and accessories at bargain prices. Sellers pay a 10% commission (capped at $50 per item) to SJAA, a tax-exempt organization, and payments for auction purchases are handled post-auction.

articles.title: School star parties Jim Van Nuland
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association's (SJAA) school star party program is highlighted as a crucial activity, with upcoming events scheduled for April and May. These events, which in March featured Mars and the Moon, will prominently feature Comet Hale-Bopp in April. The article lists specific dates, schools, and target audiences for these educational outreach opportunities, while also appealing for volunteers to assist and providing contact information.

articles.title: Be A Visiting Astronomer New NSF/NASA Program for 1997-98
articles.summary: Project ASTRO, a new NSF/NASA-funded program for 1997-98, is seeking amateur and professional astronomers and advanced astronomy students to partner with 4th-9th grade teachers in Bay Area schools. Participants will attend a summer training workshop and make at least four daytime visits during the school year to lead hands-on astronomy activities and serve as educational resources. The program aims to promote inquiry-based science education through direct engagement between astronomers and students.

articles.title: Leaky Lick Lid
articles.summary: Lick Observatory, home to the historic 36-inch Clarke refractor, is facing critical issues with its leaking dome roof due to a lack of funding from the University of California. A recent news story highlighted the problem, showing buckets collecting drips inside, though the telescope itself remains undamaged. A fund has been established to raise the estimated $18,000 needed for repairs, and tax-deductible donations are being solicited.

articles.title: Membership List Publication
articles.summary: The SJAA board plans to re-distribute a membership list, including names, addresses, and phone numbers, to its members. Members have the option to opt out entirely or customize which personal details are included in the list. This initiative aims to foster connections, help members find observing partners, and facilitate project discussions within the community.

articles.title: Fremont Peak Photo Needed
articles.summary: Ranger Rick Morales at Fremont Peak is urgently requesting a "before" photo of the southern horizon, taken from near the 30" telescope before April 1996, when new prison lights significantly increased light pollution. This image is needed to persuade prison officials, in conjunction with a future "after" photo, about the negative impact of their lights on the night sky at the Peak and advocate for mitigation.

articles.title: Promoting Darkness
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) has officially joined the International Dark Sky Association (IDA) to actively combat light pollution. Members interested in addressing light pollution issues are encouraged to connect with the board to organize efforts and leverage the club's new membership. The article also provides a link to view examples of light pollution from Soledad prison.

articles.title: Messier, continued from page 1
articles.summary: An amateur astronomer describes their ongoing Messier surveys using a 98mm Brandon telescope, a 10x50 binocular, and a 50mm Meade beginner refractor. The author notes successful observations of challenging objects like M76 and numerous galaxies in Virgo and Coma Berenices, highlighting the capability of smaller apertures. Challenges in locating objects in star-poor regions were overcome by using deep star charts and a larger telescope as an observing aid.

articles.title: Web Page Maintenance
articles.summary: Bill Arnett is seeking volunteers to help maintain the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) web page. Individuals interested in contributing to this effort should contact him via email for further information.

articles.title: Observational Astronomy Class To Focus On Moon And Mars
articles.summary: The Observational Astronomy Class recently held a successful and informative presentation on basic astrophotography by John Gleason, which was well-received and will be followed by a more advanced session later. The upcoming class on April 26 will be led by Jack Zeiders and focus on planetary observation, particularly Mars, with telescopes available for viewing. These free instructional meetings are open to everyone and have been very successful.

articles.title: Mars, Moon, Double Stars And Bright Skies
articles.summary: Jay Freeman reports on an observing session from his Palo Alto driveway on March 18, using a 6-inch Maksutov telescope. He details rewarding views of the Moon, including specific craters and rilles, and expresses a pilot's perspective on lunar terrain. Mars, however, was disappointing due to apparent atmospheric obscuration, while several double stars were successfully observed, despite light-polluted suburban skies.

articles.title: Confessions, continued from page 1
articles.summary: An amateur astronomer recounts a group observing session, likely a Messier Marathon, at Coe where participants used various instruments to find Messier objects and explore galaxies. Despite minor challenges, the session was highlighted by an unexpected and stunning view of Comet Hale-Bopp, which captivated many and led them to pause their Messier hunt. The night, filled with camaraderie and shared observations, concluded with 102 Messier objects identified and a memorable encounter with the comet.

articles.title: Directions to SJAA places
articles.summary: The article provides detailed driving directions to two observing locations for the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA): Henry Coe State Park and Fremont Peak State Park, including specific highways, mileages, and a park fee for Fremont Peak. It also includes publication details for the SJAA Ephemeris newsletter, noting its monthly publication schedule and the association's mailing address, dating the specific issue to April 1997.

articles.title: COMET COMMENTS
articles.summary: This article details the spectacular ongoing display of Comet Hale-Bopp, noting its prime evening visibility from late March through early May, coinciding with events like the partial lunar eclipse and Astronomy Day for public viewing. It also briefly announces the recent discoveries of two fainter comets, C/1996 R3 and C/1997 D1 (Mueller), with the latter potentially becoming visible to amateur astronomers later in the year.

articles.title: Ephemerides - Epoch 2000, 0h UTC
articles.summary: This document presents ephemerides for comets C/1995 O1 (Hale-Bopp), 81P/Wild 2, and 46P/Wirtanen for Epoch 2000, 0h UTC, including their Right Ascension, Declination, and magnitude for dates in April and May. It also provides detailed orbital elements for these comets. Additionally, the article announces the identification of comet C/1997 BA6 (Spacewatch) by the Kitt Peak program, noting its current distance and future perihelion.

articles.title: Celestial Calendar - Apr 1997
articles.summary: This document provides a celestial calendar for April 1997, detailing key astronomical events and observational data. It includes lunar phases with corresponding rise, transit, and set times, along with similar data for Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn. Additionally, it lists astronomical twilight times, sidereal time, and a specific date for the darkest Saturday night.

articles.title: Astro Ads
articles.summary: This document features 'Astro Ads,' a classifieds section for non-commercial sale of astronomy-related products, showcasing used Celestron C90 and Firstscope 60 EQ telescopes. It also provides guidelines for submitting new ads, which run for one month, and encourages members to submit articles for publication in the SJAA Ephemeris newsletter.

articles.title: Recent Board Actions
articles.summary: The SJAA Board of Directors is working to enroll the club into the International Dark Sky Association, an initiative expected to cost $100, and encourages interested members to contact board members. Additionally, annual officer elections were held on March 22, resulting in a new Ephemeris editor and the formation of an activities committee, with plans also underway for an SJAA picnic at Fremont Peak.

articles.title: Telescope Loaner Program Status
articles.summary: This article provides a status update for a telescope loaner program, listing various telescopes currently out on loan, their borrowers, and due dates. It also indicates which telescopes are available for reservation by members and includes contact information for reserving equipment. A notable request is made for information regarding a borrower who has not returned a telescope.

articles.title: Officers and Board of Directors
articles.summary: This document lists the officers, board of directors, and key staff members for an organization, including their names and contact phone numbers. It details roles such as President, VP, Secretary, Treasurer, and Directors, along with personnel for the Ephemeris staff (Editor, Printing, Mailing) and the Mentoring Program Chairman. The information serves as an organizational directory for leadership and program responsibilities.

articles.title: Activities Committee
articles.summary: This document lists key contacts and committee chairpersons for various activities within an astronomical association, likely the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA), as dated April 1997. It provides names and phone numbers for individuals managing activities, observational astronomy education, observatory operations, school star parties, a telescope loaner program, and the organization's web page.

articles.title: San Jose Astronomical Association Membership Form
articles.summary: This document is a membership form for the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA), detailing options for new or renewal memberships ($15 standard, $6 junior) and an optional Sky & Telescope subscription add-on ($27). It provides instructions for payment via check to "SJAA" and submission either at a meeting or by mail to the treasurer, Bob Elsberry. The form also includes contact details for the association and indicates the document's publication date as April 1997.
